name: BlurText-TS-TW
title: Blur Text
description: Two lines of type arrive out of a heavy blur, resolving word by word into crisp text with a short stagger. The reveal fires when the block scrolls into view.
use: A hero headline should appear gently as the page loads or scrolls into view.
avoid: Content that must be readable immediately: the first frame is blurred and dim.
a11y: The copy stays real text for screen readers; the blur reveal has no reduced-motion path and starts invisible. (keyboard: n-a, labels: good, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A bold white headline sits above a smaller grey subtitle, both left aligned on a black stage. Type is tight and plain, and a tiny bordered Replay control rests in the lower right.
behaves: Each word fades up from a heavy blur with a short stagger, going from soft and faint to sharp. The smaller line follows with a quicker, opposite-direction drift and the whole thing restarts on replay.
customise: Text, delay, step duration, word or letter mode, drift direction, easing and custom keyframes are props. Layout classes come through className.
weight: light: A handful of spans with filter and opacity keyframes that run once per view.
demo: Headline reads "Design systems built to last" over "Composable. Accessible. Beautiful.", with a Replay button.
issues: Some frames are almost blank because the text begins deeply blurred.
polishWhy: Crisp hierarchy and a smooth stagger; the stray Replay button adds demo clutter.
